title: Dedicated cluster: noise detection and dynamic reservation adjustments
creator: Priya Natarajan
description: Follow-up initiative after recent dedicated cluster capacity incidents. Build a detection pipeline for noisy-neighbor patterns and an adaptive reservation adjustment workflow that reduces both tail latency spikes and wasted reserved capacity. Focus on automated detection + short-term mitigations and a phased rollout of dynamic reservation resizing and adaptive throttling policies.
impact_summary: During two capacity events in Q1 2026, tenant-level noisy work caused eviction spikes and request latency regressions for high-SLA customers. Events lasted 15-45 minutes and impacted 3 paying customers with P95 latency exceedance and several failed inferences. Cost of temporary overprovisioning and manual interventions estimated at ~$30k in labor and reserved capacity waste over the prior month.
incident_timeline: 2026-02-10 02:14 UTC: First signs of eviction increase in cluster-dedicated-phi, initial alerts fired (eviction-rate, p95-latency)
2026-02-10 02:17 UTC: Oncall escalated; mitigation applied (increase reservation for affected tenant group, manual node-pool scale-up)
2026-02-10 02:45 UTC: Latency stabilized after manual action; alerts suppressed. Post-incident review raised detection gaps.

2026-03-01: Postmortem and initial action list created by SRE and Runtime teams. Decision to prototype automated detection and soft-reservation adjustments made.
2026-03-10: Prototype detection pipeline submitted for review (PR #3587).
root_cause: Combination of two factors: (1) tenant workload pattern that generates rapid concurrent large-sequence requests causing KV cache pressure and sustained GPU memory spikes; (2) reservation sizing that assumed conservative steady-state profiles without short-term elasticity leading to either eviction or unnecessary manual scale-ups. Existing burst policy allowed soft bursts but lacked quick throttling signals tied to cache-exhaustion and global GPU memory metrics.
short_term_mitigations: Introduce an SLO-based pager that correlates eviction rate, p95 latency, and GPU memory pressure to detect noise patterns within 3 minutes.
Adjust burst window down from 5 minutes to 90 seconds for tenants flagged as noisy, as a temporary policy during incidents.
Create a runbook for oncall that includes a step to toggle per-tenant soft-throttle and increase reservation by a capped percentage (max +30%) to avoid over-allocations.
Add an automated alert that surfaces recent reservation changes and who approved them to reduce manual churn.
long_term_actions: Build a streaming noise-detection pipeline using existing trace logs + metric rollups: identify tenants with concurrent high sequence-length distributions and KV miss correlation.
Implement dynamic reservation adjustments: small, frequent resizing (0-20% steps) driven by forecasted demand and validated by short A/B rollouts per tenant.
Introduce adaptive throttling that uses cache-exhaustion and model-kernel queue depth signals as inputs to backpressure decisions instead of solely relying on request rate.
Enhance cost controls: ensure dynamic resizing has hard floor and ceiling per tenant to prevent cost runaway; integrate with billing alerts for significant reservation changes.
Add canary simulations in staging that replay production traces to validate reservation and throttling policies before global rollout.

rollout_plan: Phase 1: non-customer-facing prototype in staging using last 7 days of anonymized production traces. Phase 2: opt-in beta for 3 low-risk tenants with manual rollback controls. Phase 3: gradual ramp with per-tenant hard caps and billing guardrails. Each phase gated by defined SLO metrics and a safety rollback checklist.
testing_plan: Unit tests for signal ingestion, integration tests against a mocked reservation control plane, chaos test injecting synthetic noisy tenants in staging, and a 72-hour monitor window post-deploy for any regression. Use canary trace replay to verify no increase in p99 latency.
tradeoffs: Automated resizing reduces operator toil but risks over-reserving which increases unit cost. We prefer conservative step sizes and strong guardrails. Adaptive throttling preserves cluster health but may impact tail latency for offending tenants; will expose opt-out for enterprise customers with contractual SLAs.

final_notes: Objective is to reduce incident frequency due to noisy neighbors by at least 60% and to limit peak unnecessary reservation increases to under 20% of current costs within 90 days. This ticket will track end-to-end work until the dynamic controller is in a guarded rollout and SRE runbooks are updated.
